title: Imperfect and present perfect: before and now

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the imperfect (*eran*) from A2 Unit 21 and the present perfect from A2 Unit 1. From B1 Unit 5 you also know how they contrast: the imperfect for how things used to be, the present perfect for a change that still matters now. A Cold War summary needs both: what the region was like then, and what historians have found since.

items.spanish: Antes de 1945, las universidades y los sindicatos ya tenían sus propios conflictos.
items.english: Before 1945, universities and unions already had their own conflicts.

items.spanish: Los historiadores han podido estudiar documentos que antes eran secretos.
items.english: Historians have been able to study documents that used to be secret.

items.spanish: En los últimos años se han abierto archivos en Estados Unidos.
items.english: In recent years archives have been opened in the United States.

items.spanish: Antes se veía la política como una lucha entre dos bandos; hoy los historiadores han descubierto más causas.
items.english: Before, politics was seen as a fight between two sides; today historians have discovered more causes.

sections.content: Use the imperfect for the background (*eran secretos*, *tenían*) and the present perfect for what has changed up to now (*han podido*, *se han abierto*). One sentence can have both.
